title: What is Endometrial (Uterine) Cancer? | Dr. Satinder Kaur
description: Endometrial cancer or uterine cancer is a female genital or reproductive system cancer that begins in the lining of the womb that is the uterus. It occurs mostly in women after the age of 55. Different stages of this cancer need to be treated by surgery, different therapies, and other treatments to make sure that there is no reoccurrence.   Dr. Satinder Kaur, Senior Consultant Gynaecology - Oncology at at Dharamshila Narayana Superspeciality Hospital, Delhi, shared important details on endometrial cancer. She also talked about its risk factors, diagnosis, treatment, and prevention measures of endometrial cancer.   #NarayanaHealth #HealthForAll #AllForHealth #NHCares  For video consultation with the doctor, log on to https://video.narayana.health/home  Visit our website https://www.narayanahealth.org to know more about Narayana Health and its facilities. asr.full_text: Hello, I am Dr. Sathinder Kaur Senior Consultant and Clinical Lead, Gynaeoncology, the Ramshila Narayana Superspecialty Hospital, Delhi. Endometrial cancer or the uterine cancer is a disease of the developed nations. it is usually seen in countries which have high-income groups, like U.S., Canada, Australia but is also increasing in the developing nations, because of the lifestyle changes, because of the westernization of the developing nations. The risk factors related to these diseases are diabetes that is abnormal blood sugars, increase in blood pressure that is hypertension, hypothyroidism, thyroid related diseases and the most important is obesity which leads to infertility, polycystic ovarian syndrome, problem in conception and all these lead to an abnormal hormonal balance in the body, and increased estrogen levels in the body which effect the uterine cavity and leads to the development of the cancer in the uterus. This cancer often presents earlier with abnormal vaginal bleeding. Majority of the patients almost more than 90% of the females are postmenopausal i.e. the present after the menopause with some abnormal kind of bleeding this cancer is rarely seen in young females less than 5% of the females will be less than 40 years old and they would have irregular bleeding or they would be under investigation for infertility. they would not be having period for 2-3 months may be suffering from polycystic ovarian syndrome or infertility and go to a doctor for the same problem and during a biopsy or DNC they are diagnosed to have this cancer biopsy is the must for the diagnosis of this cancer again, It does not lead to any spread of the disease without biopsy we cannot make a diagnosis and it should be done for all the patients before taking the next step biopsy tells us about the diagnosis and then patient needs an MRI or an ultrasound to see the further stage of the patient as the treatment depends upon the stage of the patient as I said this cancer presents in 90% of the patients with Early stage. Majority are Stage I patients and surgery is the treatment of choice. This is one Cancer in which the surgery can be done completely by laparoscopic or robotic means. So you will have in Early recovery and the patient can go home the next day itself with a laparoscopic or a robotic surgery This cancer does not spread by laparoscopic or robotic surgery and this is the only cancer which has shown very good survival results with this minimally invasive techniques And as I said majority are diagnosed in the first stage and therefore will not require adjuvant treatment also. But if the disease is a bit advanced stage 2 stage 3 the patient will require additional chemotherapy and radiation therapy along with surgery. This has a very good prognosis in any of the stage whether it is early or advanced and there is treatment available options available for all the stages of the disease. So when we talk about prevention there are very little preventive measures what this disease but they all are dependent on the risk factors that as discussed diabetes, hypertension, obesity and they all are related to our lifestyle. So if you have a good lifestyle, keep on walking, exercising, eat healthy food, restrain your fast foods, control your weight, you can prevent this disease for happening. Less than 10% of the patients have a familial link in this disease. So patients with this familial link usually it is called Lynch syndrome in medical terminology, would be the only patients who will require testing after 35 years of age with annual ultrasound and endometrial biopsy. Next not nobody without the genetic disorder needs any investigation or any preventative measures or any screening modalities but yes you have to be cautious any abnormal bleeding before menopause or any abnormal bleeding or even a single drop of blood after menopause is risky and you must meet your doctor and get yourself tested for this disease. You should not avoid any bleeding after menopause. Though The chances of having uterine cancer with postmenopausal bleeding is less than 10%, but it is considered to be cancer until and unless proved otherwise, so, every patient with postmenopausal bleeding must meet a doctor, get yourself evaluated, get your ultrasound done, and if required, get your biopsy also done, so that you can be protected against this dreadly disease, and get yourself that you can be protected against this dreadly disease. And get yourself vaccinated and prevent yourself against this dreadly disease and the trauma of the disease and treatment. Thank you.
